title: Indigenous democratic values
competency: Explain indigenous democratic values, name examples in Ethiopia and their roles.

keywords.def: Born in and belonging to a place and its people, not brought from outside.
A decision that everyone in the group agrees with.

en.text: Ethiopian societies have old democratic traditions: open debate, consensus and taking part in decisions. Examples are Jarsuma (Oromo), Shimigilina (Amhara), Yejoka (Gurage), Deira-Cimma (Wolayata), Enashma (Benishangul-Gumuz), Baito (Tigray), Mada'a (Afar) and Xeer (Somali). They help settle disagreements, alongside courts.

screens.title: Under the tree
screens.ask: Two neighbours in a village argue over a boundary. Elders gather under a tree to listen to both. What is this?
opts: A traditional way to settle conflict
screens.after: Many Ethiopian societies settle disputes through elders. These are indigenous democratic practices.

screens.title: 3.5 Indigenous democratic values
paras: Indigenous governance systems existed in Africa, including Ethiopia, before modern states.
Today they exist side by side with modern governance.
Traditional systems can also help the democratization process.

screens.title: Democratic traditions in Ethiopia
paras: Indigenous institutions guide social life, especially in rural areas.
They fill gaps left by formal state institutions.
Open debate, consensus and participation in decisions are old customs in many Ethiopian societies.

screens.title: Some indigenous practices
paras: These conflict resolution practices help settle disagreements. They work alongside courts.
